newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan banks' problem loans at 27.90 trln yen - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan banks' problem loans at 27.90 trln yen - MOF.

text.p: Problem loans at Japan's deposit-taking financial institutions, including small credit unions and agricultural financial firms, totalled 27.90 trillion yen as of the of March, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Friday.
Problem loans include bad loans to bankrupt firms, non-performing loans on which interest payments are in arrears for six months or more and loans being restructured.
Problem loans yet to be covered at the financial institutions were estimated at 4.69 trillion yen, MOF said in a statement.
The figures were down from 29.23 trillion yen in problem loans and 7.30 trillion yen in uncovered loans as of the end of September.

The MOF statement said Japan's 20 biggest banks held 16.44 trillion yen in problem loans as of the end of March. Annual operating profits for the 20 banks averaged a total of 3.70 trillion yen in the five years through to March 31, 1997.
Unrealised profits at all deposit-taking institutions totalled 14.03 trillion yen as of the end of March, of which the 20 biggest banks held 8.75 trillion yen, the statement said.
